statement: Prove that there is a positive integer $n$ and $2n$ non-negative real numbers $0 \leq a_1 \leq a_2 \leq \cdots \leq a_n$ and $0 \leq b_1 \leq b_2 \leq \cdots \leq b_n$ satisfying: (i) $a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_n \geq 2025^{2025}$; (ii) $b_1 + b_2 + \cdots + b_n \geq 2025^{2025}$; (iii) $c_1 + c_2 + \cdots + c_n \leq \dfrac{1}{2025^{2025}}$, with $c_i = \min(a_i, b_i)$ for $i \in \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$. Also, find the minimum $n$ for which such numbers exist.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB < AC$ and let $\Gamma$ be its circumcircle. Let $M$ be the midpoint of side $BC$ and define $D$, $E$ and $F$ as the feet of the altitudes corresponding to sides $BC$, $AC$ and $AB$, respectively. Let $N$ be the intersection of $AM$ and $EF$. Line $EF$ intersects $\Gamma$ at $R$ and $S$ such that $R$ lies on the smaller arc $AB$ of $\Gamma$ and $S$ lies on the smaller arc $AC$ of $\Gamma$. Define $T$ as the intersection of lines $BS$ and $CR$. Prove that $AD$ is the angle bisector of $\angle TDN$.

Let $(a_n)_{n \geq 1}$ be an infinite sequence of positive integers such that: (i) $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{10000}$ are pairwise distinct positive integers; (ii) for $n > 10000$, $a_n$ is the least positive integer different from $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{n-1}$ such that $|a_n - a_{n-1}|$ is a power of $2025$ (note that $1$ is a power of $2025$). Prove that every positive integer appears in the sequence.

For each positive integer $n$ define the sum $$f(n) = \lfloor \sqrt{1} \rfloor + \lfloor \sqrt{2} \rfloor + \cdots + \lfloor \sqrt{n} \rfloor.$$ Determine all integers $k$ such that there exists a positive integer $n$ satisfying $f(n) = nk$.

Let $n \geq 4$ be a positive integer and let $\mathcal{P}$ be an $n$-sided convex polygon. A set $\mathcal{X}$ of the diagonals of $\mathcal{P}$ is called \textit{blocking} if any triangulation of $\mathcal{P}$ has at least one diagonal in $\mathcal{X}$. Determine, for each $n$, the least possible number of diagonals a blocking set $\mathcal{X}$ can have.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with $90^\circ > \angle ABC > \angle CDA > \angle DAB$. Let $\mathcal{R}$ be the set of lines $\ell$ such that there is a circle tangent to all four reflections of $\ell$ over the four sides of $ABCD$. Prove that $\mathcal{R}$ can be partitioned into 8 sets such that all the lines in any one set are either all concurrent or all parallel.
